subject.title: fix(sqlite): stop mount probes blocking database startup

question: Must SQLite database opening be strictly free of synchronous external-process discovery, or is a best-effort execFileSync timeout with residual unbounded-wait risk acceptable here?
rationale: The current patch is only a mitigation under Node’s process contract; choosing whether database startup may retain that residual availability risk is an owner-level runtime-boundary decision.

options.title: Remove the startup probe
options.body: Move mount classification to an asynchronous prepared-fact boundary or conservatively select rollback mode without invoking an external command during database open.

options.title: Accept the partial mitigation
options.body: Merge the synchronous timeout only after explicitly accepting that it cannot guarantee a deadline and obtaining real-host evidence for the intended failure class.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Leave current behavior unchanged until a supported host can reproduce the blocking condition and validate a non-blocking design.

recommendation.title: Remove the startup probe
recommendation.body: Move mount classification to an asynchronous prepared-fact boundary or conservatively select rollback mode without invoking an external command during database open.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and authored the latest implementation refinements, so they are best positioned to choose the SQLite startup boundary.
